claim: The Customer DocType is described as a Buyer of Goods and Services and declares Customer Type values Company, Individual, and Partnership.
Customer links to Customer Group and Territory and separately links Customer Primary Contact to Contact and Customer Primary Address to Address.
Customer implements autoname, validate, on_update, on_trash, before_rename, and after_rename operations in its Document controller.
get_customer_name strips Customer Name and returns it as the Customer document name, adding a numbered suffix when that name already exists.

Customer exposes Disabled, which blocks use on new transactions, and Is Frozen, which blocks further accounting entries; the captured Customer metadata does not present these as one named workflow status field.
Customer lifecycle event handlers include onload, after_insert, validate, on_update, and on_trash.
Customer validation rejects a Customer Group whose is_group value is true and requires selection of a non-group Customer Group.
When Customer has a Sales Team, the total allocated contribution percentage must equal 100.
Customer validation throws Invalid Customer Group for a group-type Customer Group and throws when an Internal Customer for the represented Company already exists.
Customer onload exposes dashboard_info through set_onload, while primary Contact creation persists customer_primary_contact, mobile_no, and email_id through db_set.
Customer exposes get_customer_group_details and make_quotation through frappe.whitelist; make_quotation returns a mapped Quotation Document.
The captured controller is class Customer and imports party-account validation from erpnext.accounts.party; these bytes do not establish a separate generic Party DocType for this family.
The Item DocType is described as a Product or a Service that is bought, sold or kept in stock and is identified by required unique Item Code.
Item links Variant Of to another Item with has_variants enabled, links Item Group to a non-group Item Group, and links Default Unit of Measure to UOM.
Item implements autoname, after_insert, validate, on_update, on_trash, before_rename, and after_rename operations.
Item autoname strips Item Code and assigns it to both item_code and the document name; naming-series mode can first derive that Item Code.

Item exposes Disabled and End of Life controls: disabled Items cannot be selected in transactions, and End of Life defines the date after which the Item can no longer be used; no named Item workflow transition list is evidenced here.
Item lifecycle handlers onload, after_insert, validate, and on_update load stock and asset readbacks, create opening stock or Item Price, validate, and update variants and Item Price.
Opening Stock processing returns for a non-stock, serialized, or batched Item and otherwise requires Valuation Rate unless the Item is Customer Provided.
Item UOM conversion rows must not repeat a Unit of Measure, and the conversion factor for the Default Unit of Measure must equal 1.
Item validation throws when Customer Provided Item is also a Purchase Item or has Valuation Rate, and when Fixed Asset Item is a stock item or lacks Asset Category.
Item onload exposes stock_exists, asset_naming_series, current_valuation_method, and asset_exists through set_onload.
Item exposes get_item_details and get_uom_conv_factor through frappe.whitelist; get_uom_conv_factor documents conversion from uom to stock_uom.
The source description calls Item a Product or a Service, while the actual DocType and controller are named Item; these bytes do not justify replacing Item with a normalized Product term.
Sales Order requires a Customer and a child Items table whose options are Sales Order Item; Order Type values are Sales, Maintenance, and Shopping Cart.
Sales Order links Customer to Customer, Items to Sales Order Item, Amended From to Sales Order, and Customer Address and Contact Person to Address and Contact.
Sales Order validates, submits, cancels, updates status, creates Delivery Note, and creates Sales Invoice through named controller methods.
make_delivery_note maps Sales Order data toward Delivery Note, and the whitelisted make_sales_invoice operation accepts source_name and a target Sales Invoice document input.

Sales Order Status values are Draft, On Hold, To Pay, To Deliver and Bill, To Bill, To Deliver, Completed, Cancelled, and Closed; close_or_unclose_sales_orders closes eligible submitted orders and reopens Closed orders by update_status Draft.
Sales Order handles before_validate, validate, on_submit, on_cancel, on_update_after_submit, and before_update_after_submit lifecycle events.
Closing or reopening Sales Orders requires Sales Order write permission; closing applies only to submitted orders not already Cancelled or Closed and not both fully delivered and fully billed.
Sales Order cancellation refuses a Closed order and refuses cancellation while linked draft Sales Invoices exist.
Sales Order throws WarehouseRequired when a stock Item needs a source Warehouse, throws when a Closed order is cancelled, and throws PermissionError when close_or_unclose lacks write permission.
Sales Order onload exposes can_update_items and reserved-stock flags; cancellation persists status Cancelled through db_set, while update_status calls notify_update and clears DocType notifications.
Sales Order exposes close_or_unclose_sales_orders, make_delivery_note, make_sales_invoice, get_events, and make_purchase_order through frappe.whitelist.
Sales Order has separate Status, Delivery Status, Billing Status, and Advance Payment Status fields; their distinct native value sets are retained without deriving one normalized order state model.
